bullets.title: Soft PCE print cuts October Fed hike odds to ~37%; yield curve steepens to post-Sept highs
bullets.body: Core PCE came in at 3.01% YoY vs 3.28% forecast, with the 3-month pace at just 2.05%, sharply reducing Fed tightening urgency. October hike odds fell from ~70% Monday to ~37%; markets now price 4-5 total hikes this cycle vs analyst estimates of 2-3. The 10yr yield nonetheless rose ~6bp on stronger growth repricing, with the 5.313% level the highest since 2002 and the curve now steeper than pre-September Fed levels.

bullets.title: Q2 GDP revised to 3.2% Core (FSPDPs) but true demand closer to 2.1% trend — AI imports distort
bullets.body: Q2 GDP level revised up 60bps; 4-quarter growth revised to 1.75% with trend line now 2.1%. Core GDP (Final Sales to Private Domestic Purchasers) revised to 3.2%, but equipment capex driving the gap is systematically imported AI hardware, creating double-counting. MacDonell argues underlying demand growth is closer to the 2.1% GDP trend; productivity data likely needs upward revision, with yields now the main macro threat.

bullets.title: 10yr Treasury yields at 22-year highs driving sector rotation; Q3 saw largest quarterly bond selloff since 1994
bullets.body: UST 10yr touched 5.313%, highest since 2002, triggering major stock-bond rebalancing. September saw the largest quarterly jump in yields since 1994. Hedgeye notes Large Cap Tech (XLK +5% in Sept) masking broad weakness: Financials (XLF -7.5%), Consumer Discretionary (XLY -6.7%), Utilities (XLU -6.6%), and Industrials (XLI -4.7%) all declined. Small caps underperforming as 22-year high yields pressure sub-5yr bank financing; Russell 2000 bearish per multiple signals.

bullets.title: Futures +0.36% led by tech; MU and ACN beats provide morning catalyst; breadth remains weak
bullets.body: E-Mini S&P futures +28pts (+0.36%) and Nasdaq 100 +75bp above VWAP pre-open, with MU and ACN earnings the proximate drivers. Despite the index-level gains, breadth weakness persists with VIX-MOVE divergence flagged as a concern. JPM shifted to Tactically Bullish citing lower inflation and tech momentum; S&P risk range 7601-7790 (bullish), Nasdaq 26506-27350 (bullish), Russell 2000 2770-2871 (bearish).

bullets.title: AI capex cycle accelerating: hyperscaler spend revised to $805B in 2026, $1.1T in 2027
bullets.body: JPM sharply revised hyperscaler capex estimates to $805B for 2026 and $1.1T for 2027. Banks including SocGen and MUFG are pulling back from data center loan deals, while AI infrastructure financing tightens. Compute supply remains constrained, creating a divergence between cash-funded AI infrastructure leaders (up ~17% over 60 days) and neocloud names (down ~7%).

bullets.title: Midterm elections and regulatory creep shrinking AI-friendly data center states from 27 to ~15
bullets.body: U.S. AI data center demand estimated at 107 GW through 2030, but only ~70 GW has confirmed offtake and locations. Over 800 local moratorium/pause actions since June 2025; 16% of US counties now have regulatory restrictions. Texas (47% of announced capacity) faces ERCOT queue review in December that could impact 70-80% of state projects. The regulatory map is shrinking, which benefits companies with already-permitted capacity.

bullets.title: Oil at $92/bbl (+2%) on Iran impasse; Middle East risk remains macro wildcard on inflation and rates
bullets.body: WTI rose 1.9% to $92.09 and Brent +2.5% as no US-Iran nuclear deal is expected through midterms, with Middle East exports at 80-85% of pre-war levels. Iran has shifted from rejecting demands to proposing sequencing terms, with Qatari mediators active, but Washington's macro clock on inflation/rates is tightening faster than physical supply risk eases. Three Liberian tankers struck in Hormuz Tuesday; attribution unclear.

bullets.title: Micron crushes F4Q and F1Q guide; supply/demand tightening through CY28 with 75%+ of 2027 output committed
bullets.body: MU F4Q revenue $54.23B beat consensus $51.33B; EPS $33.42 beat $31.72. F1Q guidance $61.5B revenue (+7.1% above Street) and EPS $38.15 (+7.6%). Management expects memory supply-demand materially tighter in CY27-28 vs 2026, with >75% of 2027 output already committed via 26 Strategic Customer Agreements covering ~35% of revenue through 2030. HBM pricing for CY27 is materially above CY26 with most volume already sold; gross margin of 86.25% guided as F1Q floor with improvement expected through FY27. Buybacks resume December 9 with plans to return 100%+ of excess cash.

bullets.title: Google Gemini 4 Argon launches at frontier benchmarks but faces internal skepticism on real-world performance
bullets.body: Google released Gemini 4 Argon, which tops 14 of 19 benchmarks vs GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1, and Claude Opus 5.5, with a 1M-token output limit and introductory pricing of $2/$10 per 1M input/output tokens — significantly below Claude ($10/$50) and GPT-6 Astra. Citi views the launch as removing a key overhang and reiterates Buy at $447. However, internal engineers expressed doubts about real-world coding performance, and GOOGL shares had declined ~15% from May highs ahead of the release.

bullets.title: OpenAI Dots agents and GPT-6.1 Sol expand platform threat to MSFT and GOOGL enterprise turf
bullets.body: OpenAI launched Dots agents operating 24/7 with persistent context across 4,000+ apps, moving beyond chatbot into Microsoft and Google territory. GPT-6.1 Sol matches frontier model performance at one-fifth the cost, with cached input pricing 95% below standard. OpenAI's 1.2B weekly users and ChatGPT sign-in create a distribution platform for third-party developers, while a zero-data-retention offering challenges a key enterprise advantage Microsoft has emphasized.

bullets.title: Accenture surges ~17% on F4Q26 beat and FY27 guide; bookings inflection signals AI services durability
bullets.body: ACN F4Q revenue $18.68B beat guidance and consensus by ~4%; EPS $3.29 vs $3.19 Street. New bookings of $22.2-22.7B accelerated from -3% YoY in F3Q to +5% YoY in F4Q with a book-to-bill of ~1.19x. FY27 guidance of 3-6% CC revenue growth is 1pt better than consensus; dividend raised 4.9% to $1.71 and $11.5B returned to shareholders in FY26. Analysts view the bookings inflection as evidence AI disintermediation fears are easing and AI work is converting to durable revenue.

bullets.title: Broadcom lends Anthropic $42B for infrastructure; expands 3.5GW AI compute collaboration with Google through 2031
bullets.body: Broadcom agreed to lend Anthropic up to $42B, with debt convertible into Anthropic common stock, to finance infrastructure purchases — covering roughly one-third of Anthropic's $125B five-year TPU commitment. Broadcom also extended its long-term agreement to supply custom TPUs to Google through 2031, with Broadcom, Google, and Anthropic expanding strategic collaboration for ~3.5 gigawatts of AI compute capacity starting 2027.

bullets.title: MSFT Cloud ROIC stabilizing at 32-33% FY27-31E despite capex intensity; second-highest among hyperscalers
bullets.body: JPM estimates Microsoft Cloud ROIC at ~37% in FY26, declining from ~54% in FY24, stabilizing at 32-33% through FY31E — second only to Google (38%) among hyperscalers, ahead of Meta (31%), Amazon (18%), Oracle (13%). The A&I segment generates $136B operating income on $268B revenue with 50%+ margins. High-margin software (M365, GitHub, Security) layered onto shared GPU/CPU infrastructure is seen as the key differentiator vs infrastructure-only peers.

bullets.title: TSMC: 3Q26 revenues at high-end of guidance; N2/N3 tight through 2028; capex to hit $100B in 2028
bullets.body: TSMC expected to report 3Q26 revenues of $45.8B (+14% QoQ) at the high-end of guidance with 66.8% gross margins. 4Q26 expected +11% QoQ, limited by N3 capacity. JPM raised FY27/28 EPS by 5%/6% and projects 2027/28 capex of $86B/$100B on faster N3/N2 ramp and CoWoS expansion. Tight leading-edge wafer supply extends into 2028, with A14 production potentially pulled forward.

bullets.title: Midterm election scenarios: AI/data center buildout intact regardless; gridlock historically favors semis/software
bullets.body: JPM maps three midterm scenarios with Democrats favored to win the House (92%) and Senate (63%). AI capex momentum expected to remain intact post-midterms under all scenarios; comprehensive AI regulation unlikely to pass. Gridlock historically favors healthcare, defense, and tech (lower antitrust risk). Historically, semis (+7.2%), software (+4.2%), and tech hardware (+3.7%) outperform through the full midterm window. Options market prices only modest event premium.

bullets.title: AI traffic surging: Cloudflare logs +1,700% YoY AI-agent requests; AI traffic 6.5x faster than human traffic
bullets.body: Per Cloudflare data cited by OPCO, AI-agent request volumes are up 1,700%+ YoY, and AI traffic is growing 6.5x faster than human traffic per Fastly. This supports the CDN/edge trade thesis (AKAM, FSLY, NET) as AI shifts from training to inference and agentic workloads — expected to come into focus more sharply going forward.

bullets.title: Asia September wrap: Tech/Korea/Taiwan/Japan positive; India -7.1% as yields and dollar strengthen
bullets.body: MSCI Asia Pacific ended September -0.2% despite +53bps in US 10yr yields and a +14% oil rally, with AI trade resilience the key buffer. Taiwan +3.9%, Korea +2.2%, Japan +1.5% outperformed; India -7.1%, ASEAN -3.3%, China -4.6% lagged. Korea at 4.8x FTM PE (cheapest in region), recording fifth consecutive month of FII outflows. USD strengthened +2.0% with most Asian currencies depreciating. JPM is tactically long China H-shares, Taiwan, and China Internet (KWEB).

bullets.title: 22V Research: Long Momentum factor into earnings on AI tailwinds; beat bar lower than prior quarter
bullets.body: 22V Research notes Momentum factor valuations at median relative to S&P 1500, a lower implied bar than last quarter when average excess returns for EPS beats were negative (lowest since GFC). GDP revised to 3.2% above the ~2% speed limit. AI activity is strengthening relative to non-AI cyclicals, and AI implementation is improving fundamentals. Recommendation: long Price and EPS Momentum factor into earnings season.

bullets.title: September retail flows at 12th percentile; record inflows into TLT as retail chases long-end Treasuries
bullets.body: September was the weakest month for retail flows since December 2024, with ETF flows at the 3rd percentile. Notably, record rotation into long-end Treasury ETFs (+5.4 standard deviations), driven by TLT inflows (+6.1z) as yields hit 22-year highs. Mag 7 tech names continue to dominate single-stock retail purchases with NVDA leading semiconductor buying. Russell 2000 short interest at 99.8th percentile; retail net sellers of R2000, net buyers of R1000.

bullets.title: Credit broadly healthy despite CCC spread widening; banks easing lending standards with loan growth accelerating
bullets.body: PSC Macro notes CCC and lower-tier junk bond spreads have widened recently but do not signal systemic risk — other key credit spreads remain near historic narrows. Banks are easing lending standards and loan growth is accelerating, with bond issuance volumes growing. The JPM credit Fear & Greed Index breached oversold at 83; CDX.IG at 60bp with 30c time-value suggesting value. Key risk: rising rates on junk credits yielding >8% with a steep maturity wall approaching.
